newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Meyer opposes mixture banking, commerce.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Meyer opposes mixture banking, commerce.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Governor Laurence Meyer said he opposes further mixture of banking and commercial activities in the United States at the current time.

Speaking to reporters at a conference of the Jerome Levy Economics Institute, Meyer said he favored focusing on the consolidation of banks with other financial services before addressing proposed consolidation between banks and companies outside the financial services business.
Meyer noted those distinctions among banks, insurance and securities firms and advocated "going ahead with permissable activities," before expanding banks' purview.

"We have to decide whether it's good public policy to have further consolidation. I don't want to sort of dig my heels in and say 'never' from my perspective. I think I would certainly say 'not now,'" said Meyer.
